elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: 15.6: "either Party may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement ... to any of its Affiliates"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: 15.6: "or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets ... whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: 15.6 proviso is mutual — "either Party may assign ... to any of its Affiliates or to a successor" — so SFJ may assign without PB's consent

elements.element: Vendor consent standard: not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: 15.6 requires only "the prior written consent of the other Party"; no reasonableness qualifier appears

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: No competitor restriction anywhere in 15.6 or the redline

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "A Change of Control of PB will not constitute a breach of this Agreement and will not give SFJ any right to terminate this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: 15.6: "either Party may assign ... to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets"

15.6 contains no notice requirement for permitted successor/affiliate assignments; the only notice is the change-of-control notice in 14.2.6 ("PB will notify SFJ in writing promptly"), which does not apply to either Party's assignments

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto, neither Party will sell, transfer, assign..." — unqualified consent right

offending_extra_words: A Change of Control of PB will not constitute a breach of this Agreement
or to modify any payment or other term hereof
following the closing of such Change of Control, including
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: the redline only removes SFJ's change-of-control termination/re-pricing right. Section 15.6 remains mutual, so SFJ may still assign to its Affiliates or a successor without PB's consent, no 'not unreasonably withheld' standard was inserted for other assignments, and no prohibition on assignment to a PB competitor was added.

Fallback is also incomplete on its own terms (no written-notice mechanic for successor assignments and no reasonableness standard on consent), so the clause does not sit safely at the fallback either.

Minimality fails: operation 1 rewrites the whole of the second and third sentences of 14.2.6 (official gate: changed-character ratio 0.862 > 0.600) where deleting SFJ's discretionary termination sentence would suffice. The added 'will not constitute a breach' and 'or to modify any payment or other term hereof' language is broader protection than needed to remove the termination right.

Intent is not preserved: with the 150% Development Costs payment deleted, the surviving text still says Approval Payments 'shall be reduced by the amount previously paid to SFJ as set forth in this Section 14.2.6' and still refers to 'purchasing the Trial Data Package ... as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4' and 'following the date of such termination' logic — leaving dangling cross-references to a payment and a termination that no longer exist in 14.2.6.

Suggested fix: delete only the sentence granting SFJ the discretionary termination right (and its consequential payment sentence) with a conforming edit to the reduction proviso, and separately amend 15.6 to carve the free-assignment right down to PB (excluding assignment to a PB competitor by SFJ) and add 'which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld'.
